notes: A clean Mog Garden fetch quest. Bullets 2 and 3 are the SAME trade written twice -- bullet 2 says 'obtain and trade', bullet 3 says 'trade the three items' -- so they are one trade step, with the obtaining split out ahead of it because holding all three is the only observable thing this quest offers. The sub-bullets under bullet 2 are Mog Garden husbandry (Herb Seeds / Arborscent Seed in the furrow, Cactus Stems, the Pond Dredger, a Moblin Maze Mongers voucher) -- how to farm, not where to go, so none of them is a step and none of them names a target the addon could mark. Bullet 4 is a real step even though there is nothing to click: it is a one-game-day wait followed by a zone-in, and the cutscene fires on the zone line. Neither the day count nor the game clock is visible to the addon. Fame 'Other' is not one of the nine regions and gates nothing; the Hoe is the reward and so is not evidence.

Gnatbane is a rare harvest from Herb Seeds or Arborscent Seed in the Garden Furrow and Date from Cactus Stems, neither needing fertilizer; the Moat Carp Creel comes from the Pond Dredger, helped by a Super Baitball. The Maze Voucher 08 route (pick Claraisse on a win) is outside the Mog Garden, which is why the zone here is only mostly right.

Osker is the target of the trade at (G-7); Brutus and the chocobos are landmarks in the same sentence and Greyson is a landmark in bullet 1, and none of the three is a target. The wiki writes the zone as 'Eldieme Necropolis'; the game's name is 'The Eldieme Necropolis' and that is what is recorded. notes: Three steps of quest and three of optional reward, and the two halves are worth keeping apart. The unnumbered paragraph before bullet 1 adds a requirement the header does not carry -- fame level 3 in Abyssea - Attohwa on top of the header's level 4 in Abyssea - Vunkerl -- and neither 'avun' nor Attohwa is one of the addon's nine fame regions, so both gate nothing and only the raw string survives. The '== Further, optional rewards ==' heading sits inside the walkthrough and its bullets keep counting from 4, so no renumbering was needed; the three steps under it happen after the quest is already complete and are marked optional. Bullets 4 and 5 are one step: 'head to Abyssea - Misareaux, you are looking for Panta-Putta (A)' is the same action as trading him the Toyset. Every hand-over in this quest is a key item, which cannot go through the trade window whatever the page's wording, so they are recorded as turn-ins rather than trades. The Taru Tot Toyset is a reward and so is never evidence, and the item Jester's Hat at the end is the optional reward -- only the key item Jester's hat, granted mid-chain, is.

A straight courier run through Aht Urhgan with one item at the end. The Quest Reqs field carries two things the schema has no slot for: Aht Urhgan Mission 11, and 'Mihli Aliapoh must be present in Al Zahbi'. The mission is left out of prev because prev is fed from the Previous field; the presence condition is genuinely unobservable -- the trailing line repeats it -- so both are flags and notes and gate nothing. Bullet 5 is three actions in one and splits accordingly: get into Aydeewa Subterrane by the Bhaflau Thickets (I-7) entrance rather than the Survival Guide one, farm Aydeewa Diremites around (I-9) for the Colorful Hair, then trade it to the ??? at (H-8) at the bottom of the ramp. The Colorful Hair is both an Item Req and the one observable thing in the quest, so it is the sole evidence, sitting on the obtain step where it is acquired rather than on the trade that consumes it. Walahra Temple in bullet 3 is a building inside Aht Urhgan Whitegate, not a zone, so Nadeey keeps the Whitegate zone and the (K-7) grid.

notes: The header's giver is Lehko Habhoka in Castle Oztroja (S), but the walkthrough never speaks to him -- he turns up as a battle ally in bullet 4 who has to be kept alive -- and its first action is in a different zone entirely, examining the Mithran Bivouac in Meriphataud Mountains (S) at (I-8). That is a real disagreement rather than a door in front of the giver, so start is moved to the Bivouac and the header string kept in raw. Bullets 2 and 3 are two examines of the same Collapsing Floor with nothing between them, so they merge into one step the way Divine Might's Blank Target does: once for the cutscene, again to enter the battlefield. The Poet god's key is carried into that step as a requirement even though the page never says where it is used -- fetching it is the entire content of bullet 1 and nothing else in the quest touches it; if that is wrong it costs nothing, because you obtain it one step earlier. 'Another' Poet god's key implies the previous quest's copy is gone, which is what lets it be step 1's evidence at all, and that is why step 1 is only medium. The page never names the battlefield zone, so the fight keeps Castle Oztroja (S), its entrance. Fenrir's shifts into Karaha-Baruha and Robel-Akbel are forms of the same monster, not extra kills. Bullet 8 ends the quest by zoning into Windurst Waters (S) with no NPC named, so there is deliberately no hand-in; its sub-bullet about Romaa Mihgo is a Trust Magic unlock gated on an unrelated key item and is NOT a step -- making it one would have made the last talk of the quest look like the hand-over. The trailing line about Adieu, Lilisette is a mission pointer.

notes: Three bullets, three steps, and the interesting part is what the middle one is. You do not kill these NMs, you photograph them at close range while facing them with the Soulgauger SGR-1, and you need not even have claim -- so the six named NMs are recorded with role 'drop' because that is the nearest of the three roles the schema allows, and the note says plainly that it is a camera and not a sword. Any ONE of the six satisfies the step and the page says more may qualify, so the mob list is an OR-list the schema cannot express and is flagged rather than pretended away. The Gauger Plate is the only observable thing here and it sits on that step. Naji's linkpearl is a requirement of step 1 and is handed over there, so it can never be evidence for anything. The Azure abyssite of merit is the first-completion reward, the Black Mantle the repeat reward; neither is evidence. 'Once per Vana'diel day' is a cooldown on a repeatable quest, and the clock is not visible to the addon. Fame region 'akon' is an Abyssea zone code and gates nothing.

steps.note: southeast of Verdicial Conflux #08. The linkpearl carried over from Secret Agent Man is handed over here, so it is a requirement and never evidence.

photograph, do not kill: the shot must be at close range and facing the NM, and claim is not needed. ANY ONE of these six is enough and the page says more may qualify, so the list is neither an AND nor exhaustive. Take several in case one does not turn out.

notes: Three bullets that hide a branch. Bullet 3 is not one step but three: you go back to Sieglinde (A), and then either the gauge read red or yellow, in which case she hands you the Tube of alchemical fertilizer and you go back out to a logging point, or it read blue and she finishes the quest on the spot. The colour is a dialogue line and nothing observable, but the fertilizer key item is not -- it is exactly the thing that separates the branches, so it is step 3's evidence and the second logging-point visit is marked optional. That gets the marker right both ways round: hold the fertilizer and the mark moves out to the Logging Point, do not and it stays on Sieglinde, which is where a blue-gauge player is going anyway. Logging Point is a real interactable name and resolves; the page locates the five of them only relative to Confluxes #5, #6 and #7 and gives no grid refs at all, so grid stays null. Fame region 'amis' is an Abyssea zone code and gates nothing, and the zoning needed before a repeat is not observable.

notes: A limit-break quest that never leaves one NPC. All three steps are the Nomad Moogle in Ru'Lude Gardens at (H-5), which is one marker with readiness looking ahead across them, and that is genuinely what the page describes. Bullets 4 and 5 are not steps: bullet 4 explains that each loss lowers the number of rounds you must win, and bullet 5 is the outcome, so both fold into step 3's note. The five merit points are a hard requirement of step 2 and nothing in the packets reports merits, so they are a note and a flag rather than an item. The crest count is expressible and is: ten Kindred's Crest, singular -- the plural the page writes does not resolve. 'Nomad Moogle' is a known ambiguous name shared across many zones; the Ru'Lude Gardens zone on every step is what separates this one. The sub-bullets about Login Campaign points and Shemo's 3:1 seal exchange are shopping advice, not steps.

steps.note: the (H-5) grid comes from this bullet; the header gives none. The name is ambiguous across zones, so the zone is what pins it.
you must also hold five merit points, which nothing observable reports. Crests can come from mobs, from Login Campaign points at five points each, or from Shemo at a 3:1 seal exchange.

a rock-paper-scissors mini-game -- Raging Beast beats Silent Wind beats Soaring Dragon beats Raging Beast -- and you need five wins. Every loss drops the number of wins you need by one, so it always ends. Bullets 4 and 5 are that mechanic and the outcome, not actions.
